sources.entry: pydantic-ai - A Python agent framework for building generative AI applications with structured schemas.

summary.one_liner: Pydantic AI is a typed Python agent framework for building generative AI applications, with swappable model providers, structured outputs, and the same agent running as a CLI, web chat, voice session, or durable workflow.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes an agent loop where the model is changed by a string swap and a fallback model can be configured for provider failures. Agents take typed dependencies, function tools, and an output type, and return validated, typed results. Behavior is packaged as "capabilities" that bundle tools, instructions, hooks, and model settings, and a companion Harness package supplies prebuilt ones such as a coding agent, memory, and sub-agents. The same agent can be run from a terminal CLI, a built-in web chat, a realtime voice session, or a durable execution engine (Temporal, DBOS, Prefect, and others named in the README). It also covers standalone image generation and embeddings. Instrumentation uses plain OpenTelemetry, with one-line setup for Pydantic Logfire. Related packages named in the README are Pydantic Evals, Pydantic Graph, genai-prices, and Monty.
use_cases: build a typed LLM agent in Python
extract structured data from text into validated models
run a coding agent in the terminal
durable long-running agents on Temporal or DBOS
realtime voice assistant with tool calls
generate images with a dedicated model
trace and monitor LLM calls with OpenTelemetry
evaluate agent outputs and tool-call trajectories
notable: Typed end to end: structured outputs, typed dependency injection, and typed tools validated before code runs
Capabilities as composable units that bundle tools, instructions, hooks, and model settings
Same agent runs as CLI, web chat, realtime voice, UI event streams, or headless GitHub Actions workflow
Durable execution on multiple engines (Temporal, DBOS, Prefect, Restate, AWS Lambda, Airflow, Absurd, pgtask)
Built-in 'test' model so you can try the framework without an API key
caveats: Some features (Pydantic AI Gateway, Logfire) are separate services; Logfire is described as having a free tier, with paid tiers implied beyond it
Durable execution and voice require installing optional extras and the matching engine or provider setup
